rationale: The commissioning board faces conflicting reviews, not a lack of primary studies. An umbrella review that appraises each review, measures overlap and counts each primary study once (claim c3) is the design that resolves why reviews disagree, and it grades service-use (claim c1) and loneliness (claim c2) outcomes separately. It uses published data only, as the constraints require.
alternatives: New systematic review of primary studies (refused: duplicates existing reviews within the time available)
Local before-after evaluation of the network's link workers (refused: new data cannot be collected and the design repeats the weakness of existing evaluations)
Summarise the most recent review only (refused: would inherit its overlap and selection)
whyNotMoreComplex: Re-analysing all primary studies would take longer than the board allows and is only needed where overlap cannot be resolved from the reviews.

decision.statement: Conduct an umbrella review of systematic reviews of link worker social prescribing published from 2017, with a citation matrix to count primary studies once and separate certainty ratings for wellbeing, loneliness, consultation rates and costs, reported to the commissioning board on 26 February 2027.
decision.question: What review should the network provide to the commissioning board on link worker funding?

criteria.text: Reviews disagree and overlap heavily, so an overview that counts primary studies once could change the board's reading.
A current overview with an overlap analysis already exists.

gates.requirement: Protected GP time for the review
gates.evidence: Network board minute PCN-2026-10-07 protecting two GP sessions a week from November 2026 to February 2027, supplied by the investigator

gates.requirement: A decision forum and date for the report
gates.evidence: ICB commissioning board agenda reference ICB-CB-27-02 for 26 February 2027, supplied by the investigator

alternatives: Summarise the most recent review only
decision.note: Rests on ledger claims c1 to c3 from retrieved records; both gates are met on investigator-supplied records.

summary: Umbrella review recommended; the decision rests on three ledger claims and both gates are met.
